name: Classy Numbers
description: Let's call some positive integer classy if its decimal representation contains no more than $$$3$$$ non-zero digits. For example, numbers $$$4$$$, $$$200000$$$, $$$10203$$$ are classy and numbers $$$4231$$$, $$$102306$$$, $$$7277420000$$$ are not. You are given a segment $$$[L; R]$$$. Count the number of classy integers $$$x$$$ such that $$$L \le x \le R$$$. Each testcase contains several segments, for each of them you are required to solve the problem separately.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 10^4$$$) — the number of segments in a testcase. Each of the next $$$T$$$ lines contains two integers $$$L_i$$$ and $$$R_i$$$ ($$$1 \le L_i \le R_i \le 10^{18}$$$).
output_specification: Print $$$T$$$ lines — the $$$i$$$-th line should contain the number of classy integers on a segment $$$[L_i; R_i]$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1036C — Classy Numbers [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
